parts.label: a
parts.ask: Roller coaster carriages do multiple circuits of a track. The maximum height of a carriage is 60 m, and a carriage starts a circuit 2 m above the horizontal ground. The height is modelled by \(H = a - b(t - 20)^2\), \(t\) seconds after the start of the first circuit, where \(a\) and \(b\) are positive constants. Find a complete equation for the model.

steps.text: \(b > 0\) and \((t - 20)^2 \geq 0\), so \(H \leq a\), with \(H = a\) when \(t = 20\).

parts.label: b
parts.ask: Use the model to determine the height of the carriage above the ground when \(t = 40\).

steps.why: \(t = 40\) is as far after the peak as \(t = 0\) is before it.

parts.label: c
parts.ask: An alternative model is \(H = 29\cos(9t + \alpha)^\circ + \beta\), \(0 \leq \alpha < 360^\circ\), where \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are constants. Find a complete equation for this model.

steps.text: The largest value of \(\cos\) is 1, so the greatest height is \(29(1) + \beta\).

parts.label: d
parts.ask: The carriage moves continuously for 2 minutes. Give a reason why the alternative model would be more appropriate.
parts.method: Try the quadratic model at 2 minutes

steps.head: Now the cos model at 2 minutes

steps.why: The period, in seconds: one circuit every 40 s.
After 3 full circuits it is back at the start.

parts.answerText: The carriage does multiple circuits. The cos model is periodic, so it repeats the circuit; the quadratic goes up and down only once, then gives negative heights.

check.answers: reasoning: why a periodic model suits repeated circuits
